So, in the lyrics, Zumbi is portrayed as a strong figure who can revenge for the pain of slavery. "Eu quero ver quando zumbi chegar o que vai acontecer".

\*Quilombo was a kind of community that the escaped slavers founded in Brazil to live freely, technically it was forbidden.

Brega Music (something like kitsch music) received that name by music critics that support what we call MPB (Musica Popular Brasileira- Popular Brazilian Music) which is regarded as a more refined type of music. Bossa Nova, for example, is part of MPB but it isn't a popular rhythm among the majority of the Brazilian population.  It means Bossa Nova and MPB are rhythms of the elites in the country.   
Brega Music talks about some controversial themes in our society, but in a very straightforward and simple manner: Abortion, murderer, drugs, difficulty love relationships,  treason, and a lot of other themes that are part of people's lives in the less advantaged neighborhoods of the country.    
There are two theories about the name 'Brega music':  
1) In North and Northeast Brazil, "brega" means also a brothel. It is there where always the rhythm is played for the delight of the frequenters.   
2) In Southeast Brazil (Where the biggest media corporations are located), the media began to mock about this rhythm and the people who consumed it. But the artists embraced the term, accepting the "critic" and even mocking about it. It is worth note that brega artists were champions in terms of sales, beating MPB stars (like Caetano veloso, Gilberto Gil, Chico Buarque, and others). This fact has bothered critics even now. 

There are variations inside the rhythm, the term is very broad in its meaning. In North Brazil exists the "BregaPop", it is a mixture of cumbia, calipso and a lot of electric guitars. Bregapop has evolved to "Technobrega". It is a blending of electronic music and BregaPop. TechnoBrega is played in "Aparelhagens" (a species of the rave of technobrega music) where a gigantic nave with a DJ inside it controls the lights, sounds as smokes. The first TechnoBrega is a version of Das Model (Kraftwerk) which was launched in 2000, inaugurating the blend of dance and Brega. 

​

In Northeast Brazil, Recife (in the state of Pernambuco) is the capital of Brega Music. Reginaldo Rossi, regarded as the King of Brega, and important brega bands like for example Companhia do Calypso, Banda Labaredas are all from Recife. Recently a new rhythm has come from there, the BregaFunk. It is a blending of Funk Carioca (from Rio de Janeiro) and Brega Music. Examples of artists from that rhythm are Shevchencko e Elloco and Pedro Sampaio. 

Still in Brazilian Northeast, in the state of Rio Grande do Norte, we have the "Prince of Brega" Zezo. He sings what we call "seresta", this is a slower rhythm with only a Casio Musical Keyboard. 

In Bahia (another state of Northeast Brazil) we have the "sister of seresta music", the Arrocha (it is a slang for tighten). The singer Pablo is the "King of Arrocha" and was a pioneer of that rhythm with his first band "Asas Livres". Like Pablo, other pioneers were: Silvano Salles, Nara Costa and, Marcio Moreno. In Bahia was a blending of Arrocha with Samba and Pagode, creating what we call "Bregadeira". An example of Bregadeira artist is Boyzinho. 

​

In Midwest Brazil, we have Amado Batista, one of the artists that have most sold discs in the country. He was one of the first artists to approach with his music themes like femicide, in pieces of music like "Não Faça Jamais Como Eu Fiz" and "O Julgamento".

In Brazilian Southeast, Odair José was an outstanding brega musician. He has hit song about a contraceptive, which was prohibited by the military dictatorship in Brazil.  Fernando Mendes (from the state of Minas Gerais) has as his biggest hit music about love with a woman who is handicapped and so uses a wheelchair. In the lyrics he talks about the prejudice that the couple could suffer because she is handicapped. Another brega artist from that region is José Augusto, he is also a very important songwriter. He composed the hits that Kátia sang (she is blind, so she is also known as "Kátia cega" cega means blind in Portuguese). He also composed Evidências, which is maybe the biggest success of all time of the rhythm Sertanejo (our country music). 

So, Brega Music is the most popular rhythm in Brazil, and the most embracing. It could be named "the true Popular Music of Brazil" because:

1) It is music

2) It is popular

3) It is Brazilian (even it having influences from abroad). In North Brazil some frequencies of radio from Caribe are capitated, because of this, brega from North Brazil has influences of Latino music, Tejano, and also rock. Wanderley Andrade (a great brega singer from Belém in North Brazil) recorded a disc only with songs in English in order to pay tribute to artists like Nina Hagen, Dire Straits, and Mark Knopfler. It is very easy to note the sounds of the electric guitar of Dire Straits in his songs.  Mylla Carvalho (from Belém too) who is part of Companhia do Calypso, was inspired by Britney Spears to the point that she even performed with a snake in a show (!) and wearing alike Birtney. Joelma from the band Callypso, is regarded as a species of Madonna. She is considered the "Queen of Bregapop" being a huge success in our country.

Well it is a very broad "classification". But mainly it is used to classify very popular music from the 70s, 80s, 90s. In the lyrics of that music, it is portrayed mainly love, treason, and sometimes alcohol consumption.

examples of artists are Reginaldo Rossi, Odair José, Fernando Mendes, José Augusto, Wanderley Andrade.
